title: After an update, an admin app left open cannot download the gym's data or read an Excel file until the page is reloaded, and offline it never can
what: Downloading the gym's data and reading an Excel file for import both fetch an extra piece of the admin app only when pressed. Each update renames that piece and removes the old one, and nothing tells an open tab to reload. So a desk that keeps the admin app open across an update presses Download and gets 'Could not make the file. Try again' every time, or picks a good Excel file and is told to open it in Excel and save it again. The offline keeper also throws that piece away each time it saves the app, so with no internet these two buttons never work.
expected: An open tab notices a newer version and asks for a reload (or reloads itself) before these buttons fail; the failure message says to reload, not to fix the file; the offline copy keeps the pieces these buttons need.
how_often: after every update while a tab stays open; always offline
fix_line: Tell an open tab to reload when a new version is out, say 'reload' in these two errors, and keep their pieces offline

title: A gym's web page stays up for good after the gym stops using MettleUp, showing old prices and 'Open now'
what: A gym's web page is hidden only when the gym is suspended, the owner unpublishes it or HQ switches it off. A gym whose trial ended, that stopped paying, or that has closed but was never suspended keeps its page with the last prices, timings and 'Open now', with no date saying when it was last changed. Visitors can call or walk to a gym whose prices or hours are long wrong. The page holds its last-changed date but never shows it.
expected: A page not changed for a long time, or of a gym that has left MettleUp, is hidden or shows 'Last updated' with the date, so visitors know how old the facts are.
how_often: every gym that leaves without being suspended
fix_line: Show the last-updated date on the page and hide pages of gyms that left or went quiet for months

title: A gym's web page left open keeps saying 'Open now' after the gym has closed for the day
what: 'Open now', 'Closes soon' and 'Closed now' are written into the page when it is opened. Nothing on the page updates them later, so a visitor who opened the page in the evening and looks again after closing time, or comes back to the tab the next morning, sees the old state.
expected: The page recomputes open or closed when it comes back on screen or once a minute.
how_often: whenever a tab stays open across a change
fix_line: Recompute the open or closed line in the page when the tab comes back

items.reason: Fresh install keeps the page at once; network first and no-cache on the page and worker means an update reaches every device; old caches are cleared on activate; the old address hands its sign-in over. Fault: on-demand pieces after an update and offline. Sideload vs Play and watch vs phone do not apply to web pages.

Plan or trial end hides only Become a member (Ask a question stays, already FN-B-switch-web-pages-01); suspended hides the page within about 6 minutes of edge keeping; other closed or left gyms stay up (02); open status frozen in an open tab (03). India date strings make year end and leap day safe; the chat resets after 90 days so a 6-month return starts fresh. Staff leaving, member returning and owner changing phone hold no state on these public pages.
New-only changes here: the new address, the join.mettleup.fit links and the longer never-keep list of the offline keeper. Old desks, old printed links and installed devices are all covered.

Old address keeps serving the admin app and hands the sign-in across; app.mettleup.fit still serves every old join and check-in link; the offline keeper is re-checked on every visit so installed devices get the new list.
A path exists for each; no finding.
Searched the marketing sites, gym page, join, check-in, friend and get-app pages: no new-since-last-visit marks, dots or update notices; 'new record' text is product copy, not a mark.
No new marks in this area, so none can be wrong for a first-time visitor.
